question: Do neural networks trained on conjunctive tasks contain sparse weight subnetworks that selectively implement known constituent subroutines and can be removed without destroying the paired subroutine?

key_findings.claim: Structural compositionality is operationalized as a paired sufficiency-and-complement test for investigator-specified subroutines, not as behavioral compositional generalization.
key_findings.evidence: For a model trained on C = SR1 & SR2, a target mask must yield higher accuracy on target-subroutine than other-subroutine examples, while its complement must reverse that difference. The authors explicitly distinguish this internal-structure question from generalization and leave their relationship unresolved.

key_findings.claim: The recovered mask is trained after the fact with direct labels for the desired constituent and its hyperparameters are selected to maximize the expected ablation signature.
key_findings.evidence: Continuous sparsification freezes the base weights but optimizes a sigmoid-relaxed weight mask on a separately constructed target-subroutine task. For every base-model/subroutine pair, 24 learning-rate, initialization, and start-layer configurations are screened; candidates must reach 90 percent target-task accuracy, then the validation configuration maximizing Other-minus-Target complement accuracy is chosen. Final diagnostic test sets are separate, but the measurement is still engineered and selected for the desired causal pattern rather than discovered independently.

anchors.section: Appendix C, Selection score and compute

key_findings.claim: ResNet-family and BERT-Small results frequently have the expected signs, but modularity is heterogeneous across tasks, constituents, architectures, and seeds.
key_findings.evidence: Inside-Number gives strong paired signs for both ResNet50 constituents, while Number-Contact localizes Contact but not Number; several ablation tests in Table 1 are nonsignificant. WideResNet broadly reproduces the pattern, but every tested ViT configuration fails the 90 percent base-task threshold and is excluded. The supported conclusion is asymmetric localization in some controlled settings, not universal task decomposition.

key_findings.claim: The appendix contradicts the main-text footnote that all trained base models exceed 99 percent, and it exposes material failures inside the pretraining comparison.
key_findings.evidence: The footnote on page 4 says all models eventually achieve above 99 percent, yet Table 2 reports one ResNet50 Inside-Contact seed at 75.9 percent and Figure 4 marks it gray. Table 3 reports two of three language-pretrained BERT seeds at only 65.5 and 63.5 percent on singular anaphora, even though the text characterizes language pretraining as producing more reliable modular subnetworks. These models cannot support a downstream decomposition claim because they did not learn the base task.

key_findings.claim: Random-network controls show why target-mask sufficiency alone is not evidence that the trained base model used the recovered computation.
key_findings.evidence: A mask optimized over frozen random ResNet50 or BERT-Small weights can still solve the supervised target subroutine. Random ResNet complements collapse both partitions and random BERT complements often show the wrong causal sign, so paired ablation is informative. However, trained-versus-random subnetwork coefficients are nonsignificant for most vision pairs, and random controls reuse hyperparameters selected on trained models rather than undergoing an equally favorable null search.

key_findings.claim: The reported significance levels are fragile because the cluster-robust models have only three independent base-model clusters and no multiplicity correction.
key_findings.evidence: Three masks are fit inside each of only three base-model seeds, and the GLMs cluster observations by base model. Cluster-robust asymptotic z and chi-square inference with three clusters is not reliable without small-cluster correction or randomization inference. The paper runs separate tests across many architecture-task-subroutine combinations, reports values as small as p < .001, and does not report a family-wise or false-discovery correction.

key_findings.claim: Mask size, eligible layers, and repeatability vary by orders of magnitude, so a discovered mask is not a stable or unique module boundary.
key_findings.evidence: The selected mask can begin at stage or layer 0, 3, or 4 and ranges from thousands to millions of active weights across seeds and subroutines. The overlap analysis is performed on one selected Inside-Number ResNet50 for which both masks happen to start at the same layer; Inside masks overlap near ceiling, Number masks much less, and no density-matched null or cross-model analysis is supplied. Biases are never masked, so mask and complement are not a complete disjoint partition of the computation.

key_findings.claim: The experiments establish selective maskability for toy conjunctions, not reusable symbolic routines or an alternative to symbolic mechanisms in general.
key_findings.evidence: Vision stimuli contain only three hand-designed binary factors under a pairwise-embedding odd-one-out head. Language nouns of interest are always the second token and can be solved by an acknowledged positional heuristic. ResNets replace BatchNorm with InstanceNorm and are trained without dropout because dropout makes ablations more robust; no held-out recombination, cross-context mask reuse, larger language model, natural compositional task, or scaling study is run.

method.core_idea: Train a model on a known conjunction, then ask whether a sparse target-supervised weight mask is selectively sufficient for one constituent and whether its complementary weights selectively preserve the other constituent.
method.mechanism: Construct odd-one-out datasets for conjunctions of Inside, Contact, Number, subject/verb number, or antecedent/pronoun number. Train three base seeds for modified ResNet50, WideResNet50, or BERT-Small; freeze them; optimize annealed continuous-sparsification masks with an L0-style penalty on separately labeled constituent tasks; select configurations by validation complement selectivity; evaluate mask and inverse mask on held-out target- and other-subroutine test partitions; then compare scratch, pretrained, random-weight, pruned, and repeated-mask conditions.
assumptions: The investigator knows the correct constituent decomposition and can generate separately supervised data for every subroutine.
A fixed subset of weights is the right unit of modularity rather than an input-conditional activation circuit or distributed representation.
A post-hoc target-trained mask recovers a computation used by the base model rather than synthesizing an alternative readout through redundant frozen features.
Complementary weight ablation is interpretable despite nonlinear interactions, shared infrastructure, residual paths, unmasked biases, and normalization.
Target and other diagnostic partitions are equally difficult apart from which subroutine is needed.
The selected start layer and sparsity budget do not predetermine which constituent appears localized.
Three base-model seeds adequately support clustered statistical inference and model-level generalization.
Modified ResNets, a four-layer BERT, and hand-generated conjunctions are informative about ordinary contemporary networks.
A sparse selectively causal mask implies a constituent representation rather than merely a task-specific shortcut.
Internal structural decomposition bears on the need for explicit symbolic mechanisms even without demonstrating cross-context reuse or systematic generalization.

techniques.role: Requires both target-selective sufficiency of a mask and reverse-selective behavior of its complement.
Learns a near-binary weight mask through an annealed sigmoid relaxation and an L0-style sparsity term.
Builds base, constituent-training, validation, and test odd-one-out sets from controlled binary factors.
Selects learning rate, initialization, and first masked stage separately for every model and constituent.
Trains the same kind of target mask over frozen random weights to expose hidden-subnetwork confounds.
Contrasts scratch initialization with SimCLR-pretrained vision weights or pretrained BERT-Small weights.
Measures per-layer intersection-over-union among repeated masks for one selected model.
Tests accuracy differences with model-clustered GLMs, albeit with only three clusters.

evaluations.setting: Modified ResNet50 and WideResNet50 on Inside-Contact, Inside-Number, and Number-Contact visual conjunctions.
evaluations.metric: Target-minus-other accuracy for each learned subnetwork and its complementary ablation, with accuracies censored to the interval from chance to one.
evaluations.result: Expected signs appear often but not uniformly; some constituents have selective complements, Number can remain diffuse, and one ResNet50 seed fails its base task.
evaluations.baseline: Zero selectivity, the paired constituent, WideResNet replication, and random-weight mask controls.

evaluations.setting: BERT-Small on singular and plural subject-verb agreement and reflexive-anaphora template tasks.
evaluations.metric: The same paired accuracy differences, collapsed across singular and plural variants in model-clustered GLMs.
evaluations.result: Target masks are frequently selective and several complement effects have the expected sign, but mask sizes and seed effects are large and the tasks permit shallow lexical-position heuristics.
evaluations.baseline: The other constituent, zero difference, and randomly initialized BERT-Small masks.

evaluations.setting: SimCLR-initialized ResNet50 and language-model-pretrained BERT-Small fine-tuned on the controlled conjunctions.
evaluations.metric: Magnitude and consistency of mask and complement selectivity across seeds.
evaluations.result: No obvious vision benefit is visible; pretrained language models show more consistent complement patterns among successful models, while two pretrained singular-anaphora base seeds fail badly.
evaluations.baseline: Architecturally matched models trained from scratch.

evaluations.setting: Six- and twelve-layer ViTs over a grid of four learning rates and two batch sizes.
evaluations.metric: Base-task validation accuracy relative to the 90 percent inclusion threshold.
evaluations.result: Every ViT is excluded, with the best cell reaching about 86 percent on one task and substantially less on the others.
evaluations.baseline: The authors' predeclared base-task threshold and ResNet-family performance.

evaluations.setting: Random frozen ResNet50 and BERT-Small networks, plus three pruned Number-Contact ResNet50 models.
evaluations.metric: Mask sufficiency and complement selectivity under the same diagnostic partitions.
evaluations.result: Random weights support target classifiers after mask training but generally fail the expected complement pattern; pruned trained models broadly retain the Number-Contact signature.
evaluations.baseline: Task-trained dense base models and their selected mask configurations.

evaluations.setting: One selected Inside-Number ResNet50 whose two subroutine masks begin at the same stage.
evaluations.metric: Layerwise multi-mask intersection-over-union within each constituent and between constituent intersections.
evaluations.result: Inside masks are highly repeatable, Number masks are less stable, and cross-constituent overlap is lower, but no density-matched null or second model is evaluated.
evaluations.baseline: Within-constituent versus between-constituent overlap in the same base model.

limitations: Author-stated: the investigator must specify the candidate subroutines in advance; the method does not discover a decomposition unsupervised.
Author-stated: causal ablations and control models are necessary, and the recovered subnetworks are not guaranteed to be necessarily causally implicated.
Author-stated: the relationship between structural compositionality and behavioral compositional generalization is unresolved.
Reviewer inference: target-subroutine supervision can carve a new classifier from redundant frozen features rather than recover the base model's original algorithm.
Reviewer inference: hyperparameters are selected using the desired validation-set complement score, creating a strong researcher-and-search degree of freedom even though final test sets are separate.
Reviewer inference: the random-weight null reuses configurations optimized for trained models rather than applying an equally favorable hyperparameter search to the null condition.
Reviewer inference: cluster-robust z and chi-square tests based on only three model clusters do not justify the reported asymptotic p-values.
Reviewer inference: multiple task, architecture, subroutine, and control tests receive no multiplicity correction.
Reviewer inference: clamping every below-chance accuracy to chance censors reversals and changes the distribution used in differences and significance tests.

Reviewer inference: one ResNet seed and two pretrained BERT singular-anaphora seeds fail the base task, contradicting or qualifying the claims of uniformly high accuracy and more reliable pretraining.
Reviewer inference: mask sizes vary by orders of magnitude and eligible layers vary across model-subroutine pairs, so localization strength is not compared at a matched sparsity or support budget.
Reviewer inference: only weights are masked; biases and earlier unmasked stages remain active, so the mask and complement are not self-contained disjoint computational modules.
Reviewer inference: the one-model overlap analysis is selected for compatible start layers and lacks density-matched random-mask, cross-seed-model, or cross-architecture baselines.
Reviewer inference: ResNets replace BatchNorm with InstanceNorm and omit dropout specifically because dropout makes ablations more robust, limiting claims about standard training regimens.

Reviewer inference: SimCLR on the same synthetic visual distribution and large-corpus language-model pretraining are not comparable interventions, so their domain difference cannot isolate a general pretraining effect.
Reviewer inference: the language templates place the relevant noun in the second token and explicitly admit a positional shortcut; the vision tasks use only three hand-designed binary factors.
Reviewer inference: the dot-product odd-one-out head already imposes a pairwise comparison structure that may encourage separable factor detectors.
Reviewer inference: no held-out combinations, function reuse in a new task, natural-distribution benchmark, large foundation model, or scaling axis is tested.
Reviewer inference: the complete mask search costs roughly 2,448 GPU-hours beyond about 300 GPU-hours for the selected main runs, making the diagnostic unusually expensive.
failure_modes: A supervised mask finds a lottery-ticket classifier that was available in frozen weights but was never used by the trained base model.
Distributed redundant routes cause the complement to retain the target behavior, yielding a false negative for a genuinely factorized representation.
Shared infrastructure causes a complement ablation to damage both constituents, conflating modular computation with generic feature extraction.
Searching start layer and mask initialization until validation ablation selectivity is maximal overstates module evidence on a small diagnostic distribution.
A failed base model is omitted or colored gray, making the surviving architectures appear more broadly compositional than the full experiment.
Unmasked biases or residual pathways carry task information and make a reported weight subnetwork appear more self-sufficient than it is.
A very large mask is described as a sparse module even though its size and ablation damage are not matched to another constituent.
Three masks from one base model converge to different equivalent implementations, making a single module boundary nonidentifiable.
A template-specific factor detector localizes cleanly but does not transfer when the constituent moves position, changes vocabulary, or appears in a new conjunction.
Below-chance behavior is clamped away, hiding a systematic reversal that would challenge the selectivity interpretation.
A standard architecture appears negative only because its base-task optimization grid is inadequate, as in the excluded ViT condition.
A model contains selective constituent masks yet fails to recombine or reuse them on any unseen composition.
reusable_insights: Pair sufficiency with selective necessity; a probe or trained mask alone is not evidence for the mechanism used by the intact model.
Run mask discovery on frozen random networks because overparameterized random weights can contain trainable target subnetworks.
Separate constituent supervision, hyperparameter selection, and final causal evaluation into disjoint datasets.
Apply the full search budget to null controls or otherwise account for unequal optimization opportunity.
Treat module identity as an equivalence class and report stability across mask seeds, model seeds, checkpoints, and architectures.
Match sparsity, eligible layers, and ablated parameter magnitude when comparing constituent localization.
Distinguish decodability, sparse sufficiency, selective necessity, causal abstraction, cross-context reuse, and behavioral compositional generalization.
Count independent trained models rather than nested mask fits when designing statistical inference.
Include base-task failures in the conclusion instead of conditioning the architecture claim on successful learners.
Test a recovered constituent by reusing the frozen mask in a new conjunction or context without retraining it.
Use density-matched overlap nulls and avoid interpreting raw IoU as semantic modularity.
Preserve below-chance results and predefine the effect statistic rather than censoring inconvenient directions.
open_questions: Can candidate subroutines be discovered without investigator-provided labels or a hand-specified factorization?
Does a target mask remain sufficient and necessary when the same constituent appears in a new conjunction, order, vocabulary, domain, or output format?
Can causal-abstraction tests distinguish the base model's original computation from an alternative route synthesized by mask optimization?
What null jointly matches random weights, mask-search compute, support layers, sparsity, and target supervision?
How should modularity be defined for input-conditional activation circuits rather than a single fixed weight subset?
Do structural selectivity and systematic compositional generalization causally covary across training checkpoints and model scale?
Would dropout, weight decay, BatchNorm, modern transformers, and ordinary pretraining preserve the reported complement signature?
How many independently trained models are needed for calibrated model-cluster inference, and do the findings survive permutation tests and multiplicity correction?
Can equivalent sparse modules be characterized without assuming a unique parameter-space boundary?
Can circuit discovery achieve comparable faithfulness without thousands of GPU-hours of constituent-specific mask search?
Which base-task failures reflect optimization, architecture, or absence of a decomposable solution?
Does pretraining improve modularity independently of base accuracy, margin, redundancy, and the amount of prior exposure to the target factors?

competitive_landscape.title: Are Neural Nets Modular? Inspecting Functional Modularity Through Differentiable Weight Masks
competitive_landscape.difference: Csordas et al. introduce differentiable binary weight masks for functional specialization and report limited module reuse across SCAN and mathematics partitions. Lepori et al. add complementary ablations and target constituents inside one conjunctive task, but inherit the supervised-mask and reuse-identification problem.

competitive_landscape.title: Can Subnetwork Structure Be the Key to Out-of-Distribution Generalization?
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. use modular subnetwork introspection and Modular Risk Minimization to find invariant subnetworks and improve OOD performance. The reviewed paper gives a sharper paired constituent-ablation test but never connects its masks to held-out recombination or OOD benefit.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal Abstractions of Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Geiger et al. align neural states to variables in a high-level causal model and verify them with interchange interventions on compositional NLI. This yields a stronger semantic causal criterion but assumes an alignment; Lepori et al. search parameter subsets without a location assumption but recover a weaker, nonunique mask.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Interventions in Language Models with Differentiable Masking
competitive_landscape.difference: De Cao et al. optimize sparse neuron interventions tied directly to language-model output changes for subject-verb agreement and gender bias. Lepori et al. mask weights, broaden to vision, and add a paired complement test, but use synthetic four-way tasks and a much larger per-function search.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Modularity in Pre-trained Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. study neuron specialization, function-based expert grouping, causal activation perturbations, and modularity emergence across pretraining. It covers a broader transformer-pretraining trajectory, while Lepori et al. provide a cleaner constituent-conjunction intervention but only on a four-layer BERT and fixed endpoints.

competitive_landscape.title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
competitive_landscape.difference: Dziri et al. analyze multiplication, logic-grid, and dynamic-programming computation graphs and find behavior consistent with linearized subgraph matching plus rapidly degrading autoregressive correctness as composition depth grows. This is contemporaneous large-model evidence for the template-like alternative that motivates Lepori et al.; it does not prove that every sparse mask is epiphenomenal.

competitive_landscape.title: SLOG: A Structural Generalization Benchmark for Semantic Parsing
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu et al. test 17 recursion and filler-gap generalization cases beyond the mostly lexical COGS split and report large failures for pretrained transformers relative to a structure-aware parser. SLOG operationalizes structural composition behaviorally and much more strictly than binary conjunction masks, while offering no parameter-level causal localization.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles
competitive_landscape.difference: Wiedemer et al. derive support and architecture conditions sufficient for held-out compositional generalization from a data-generating-process view. That directly formalizes the behavioral outcome left open by Lepori et al., while saying less about sparse causal implementation.

competitive_landscape.title: Circuit Compositions: Exploring Modular Structures in Transformer-Based Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Mondorf et al. extract circuits for ten string-edit operations and test overlap, cross-task faithfulness, reuse, and set-operation composition into more complex functions. It directly addresses whether constituent circuitry transfers and combines, a decisive test absent from Lepori et al., though still in a synthetic grammar setting.

competitive_landscape.title: Hypothesis Testing the Circuit Hypothesis in LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: Shi et al. formalize behavior preservation, localization, and minimality as hypothesis tests and find that discovered transformer circuits satisfy them unevenly. Those explicit nulls and minimality criteria are stricter than interpreting a selected sparse mask and complement as a module.

competitive_landscape.title: Discovering Knowledge-Critical Subnetworks in Pretrained Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Bayazit et al. use multi-objective differentiable masking over weights or neurons to remove relational knowledge while preserving unrelated behavior at GPT-2 scale. It strengthens the preservation objective and scale, but localizes knowledge collections rather than testing composition and reuse of constituent computations.

competitive_landscape.title: Analyzing the Inner Workings of Transformers in Compositional Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Kumon and Yanaka find a transformer subnetwork that generalizes better than the full model and causally analyze its syntactic features, yet show that the subnetwork still relies partly on a non-compositional algorithm learned early. This directly demonstrates that subnetwork existence, selectivity, and even improved OOD behavior do not by themselves identify a purely compositional mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Syntax Without Planting Trees: Understanding Hierarchical Generalization in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Ahuja et al. compare training objectives on five controlled syntax datasets and use pruning to reveal subnetworks implementing different generalization behaviors inside one transformer. Multiple competing algorithms within the same weights qualify any inference that one recovered mask is the model's unique or dominant solution, while the objective effects sharpen the present pretraining claim.

competitive_landscape.title: Data Drives Unstable Hierarchical Generalization in LMs
competitive_landscape.difference: Qin, Saphra, and Alvarez-Melis show that syntactic complexity and tree diversity determine hierarchical versus n-gram learning, with intermediate regimes producing oscillations and cross-seed instability. This supplies a concrete data-distribution explanation for task and seed heterogeneity that a fixed endpoint mask analysis cannot isolate.

competitive_landscape.title: Identifying Sparsely Active Circuits Through Local Loss Landscape Decomposition
competitive_landscape.difference: Chrisman et al. decompose local loss gradients into low-rank parameter-space subnetworks, validate recovery on ground-truth toy circuits, and test sample-selective perturbations on transformer and convolutional models. This reduces dependence on one binary target mask, though its real-model semantic guarantees remain exploratory.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling can lead to compositional generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Redhardt et al. vary data and model scale, test held-out task compositions, prove a linear-neuron approximation result for a task family, and relate successful generalization to linear constituent decodability. It studies the scale and behavioral axes missing here, though decodability is weaker causal evidence than selective ablation.

competitive_landscape.title: Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
competitive_landscape.difference: Arora et al. use end-to-end gradient attribution and causal steering to identify roughly one hundred MLP neurons controlling subject-verb agreement and small neuron sets for latent multi-hop steps, without training a mask per target. It supplies stronger current scale and steering evidence for sparse language circuits, but does not directly test constituent reuse.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Standard neural networks often decompose conjunctive tasks into modular constituent subnetworks, and language-model pretraining makes that structural compositionality more consistent, suggesting explicit symbolic mechanisms may be unnecessary.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper contributes a concrete paired target-mask and complement-ablation diagnostic over three visual conjunctions and two language-agreement families, with modified ResNet50, WideResNet50, BERT-Small, random-weight controls, pretrained conditions, pruned models, and a limited overlap audit.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the paired sufficiency-and-complement test for known constituents inside one conjunctive task, extending differentiable-mask modularity work across two modalities. It is real evidence that some toy constituents are asymmetrically localized in trained weights. The stronger anti-symbolic interpretation is unsupported: constituent labels and decomposition are supplied, search selects for the desired ablation pattern, several base models or comparisons fail, inference uses only three model clusters, mask boundaries are unstable, and no systematic generalization, mask reuse, natural task, scale trend, or unique original mechanism is demonstrated. Later causal-circuit, reuse, and scaling work directly targets these missing criteria.
